cultura.name: El Candombe
cultura.description:
Afro-Uruguayan drum tradition brought by enslaved West African people in the 18th century.
UNESCO-listed intangible heritage — its three drums (chico, repique, piano) define carnival.

cultura.name: La Murga
cultura.description:
Satirical theatrical choir that performs social commentary through song during carnival.
Choirs of up to 20 people in elaborate costumes lampoon politicians and society.

cultura.name: La Cultura Criolla
cultura.description:
Uruguay's gaucho tradition blends Spanish, indigenous, and African roots into a rural identity.
Semana Criolla every Easter showcases horse skills, boleadoras, and folk song.

cultura.name: El Tango Oriental
cultura.description:
Tango was born on both banks of the Río de la Plata — Montevideo shares its origins.
Carlos Gardel, tango's greatest icon, was born in France but raised in Montevideo.

india_traveller.visa_note: Indian passport holders do not require a tourist visa for Uruguay for stays up to 90 days — one of South America's most welcoming countries for Indian travellers. Carry proof of accommodation and return ticket. There is no Indian consulate in Uruguay; the nearest is in Buenos Aires.
india_traveller.flight_note: No direct or easy single-stop flights from India to Uruguay. The most practical routes fly to Buenos Aires (EZE) via Dubai, Doha, or Madrid, then take a 45-minute flight or a 3-hour ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. Total journey from India takes 22–28 hours.
india_traveller.cost_per_day_inr: Uruguay is moderately priced for South America. Budget travellers can manage on ₹3,500–5,500/day in Montevideo. Punta del Este is premium — expect ₹8,000–14,000/day in peak season. Asados and set-lunch menus (menú del día) offer the best value at around ₹700–1,200.
india_traveller.veg_tips: Uruguay is a beef-heavy country, but Montevideo has a growing vegetarian scene. Safe options include tortas fritas (fried dough), cheese empanadas, salads, pasta, and pizza. Ask for 'sin carne' (without meat). Barrio Pocitos in Montevideo has several vegetarian-friendly restaurants. The alfajores (caramel biscuits) are a sweet vegetarian treat nationwide.
